:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.6`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/usePackageJsonCpu`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule doesn't have a fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`package-json/require-cpu`](https://eslint-plugin-package-json.dev/rules/require-properties/require-cpu)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"usePackageJsonCpu": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Require the `cpu` field in `package.json`.

The `cpu` field lists the processor types that a package can run on, such as `x64` or
`arm64`. Package managers read it to avoid installing the package on a processor that the
package doesn't support. Without the field, the package is installed on every processor,
and a package that can't run there fails later, when it is used.

This rule reports a `package.json` file whose outermost object has no `cpu` field. A `cpu`
field inside another object doesn't count. The rule doesn't check the value of the field.

## Examples

### Invalid

```json title='package.json'
{
    "name": "my-package",
    "version": "1.0.0"
}
```

### Valid

```json title='package.json'
{
    "name": "my-package",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "cpu": ["x64", "arm64"]
}
```
